description.value: This cross-sectional study investigated disease-specific functional brain network architecture in early-onset Alzheimer disease and behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia using resting-state fMRI graph analysis and connectomics, compared with healthy controls.

spans.text: To investigate functional brain network architecture in early-onset Alzheimer disease (EOAD) and behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD).

value: We predicted a marked pattern of network alterations including both interhemispheric and intrahemispheric connections within and outside the DMN in patients with EOAD, reflecting their multidomain cognitive and behavioral impairments.
On the other hand, bvFTD would be characterized by a focal disconnectivity involving intrahemispheric, frontotemporal connections.

Thirty-eight patients with a diagnosis of bvFTD,  37 patients with a diagnosis of probable AD  and age at onset <65 years (EOAD), and 32 age-matched healthy controls were recruited consecutively at the Scientific Institute and University Vita-Salute San Raffaele, Milan ( table 1 ).

Thirty-eight patients with a diagnosis of bvFTD,  37 patients with a diagnosis of probable AD  and age at onset <65 years (EOAD), and 32 age-matched healthy controls were recruited consecutively at the Scientific Institute and University Vita-Salute San Raffaele, Milan ( table 1 ).

Relative to controls, patients with EOAD showed severe global functional network alterations (lower mean nodal strength, local efficiency, and clustering coefficient, and longer mean path length) ( table 2 ).

spans.text: Patients with bvFTD showed no global network abnormalities relative to controls ( table 2 ). Compared with controls, patients with bvFTD were characterized by a reduced intrahemispheric between-lobe LCW linking temporal, frontoinsular, parietal, and sensorimotor lobes bilaterally; reduced interhemispheric LCW between left and right temporal lobes; and increased interhemispheric LCW of left and right parietal lobes with basal ganglia and right sensorimotor and basal ganglia areas (  p   = 0.02;  figure 2  and table e-3).
